chunks: Al-Hakim, Abu al-Hasan, Abd al-Hamid, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, the jurist, told us, narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr al-Dhari narrated to us, saying: 'Ubad ibn 'Ubad al-Mahlabi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tamimi, from his father, who said:

We were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and a cloud arose, so they said: O Messenger of Allah, this is a cloud that has arisen. He said: How do you see its foundations? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful they are and how firm their hold. He said: How do you see its branches? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful they are and how dense their accumulation. He said: How do you see its blackness? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful it is and how intense its blackness. He said: How do you see its circle? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful it is and how round it is. He said: How do you see its lightning, is it hidden, or a flash, or does it cut with a cut? They said: O Messenger of Allah, rather, it cuts with a cut. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Al-Haya (Fertility/Modesty). They said: O Messenger of Allah, how eloquent you are, and we have not seen anyone more eloquent than you. He said: And what prevents me from that, when the Qur'an was revealed in my tongue, 'in a clear Arabic tongue'.

key_terms.الْحَيَا: Al-Haya (Fertility or Modesty, contextually referring to the rain's fertility or the cloud's demeanor)
key_terms.بَوَاسِقَهَا: its branches (upper parts of the cloud)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad ask his companions about the cloud and how did he explain his eloquence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* illustrates the Prophet’s mastery of descriptive eloquence by engaging companions in a detailed observation of a cloud’s structure, culminating in the term 'Al-Haya' (often interpreted as modesty or the cloud's veiling nature). He grounds his linguistic precision in the divine revelation, citing that the Qur'an was revealed in his own clear Arabic tongue, thereby validating his speech as an extension of the Qur'anic style. This narrative serves as a key text in Shia scholarship for understanding the linguistic miracle of the Prophet and the connection between natural phenomena and divine speech.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by al-Hakim, Abu’l-Hasan, Abdul-Hamid bin Abdul-Rahman bin Hussain al-Naisabouri, the jurist, that he said: We were told by Abu Sa’eed, that he said: We were told by Ubaidullah bin Muhammed bin Sulayman al-Hashimi, that he said: We were told by Abu Amru al-Dhareer, that he said: We were told by ‘Ubad bin ‘Ubad al-Mahbali, from Musa bin Muhammed bin Ibrahim al-Tamimi, from his father, that he said:

We were at the place of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and a cloud arose, so they said: O Messenger of Allah, this is a cloud that has arisen. He said: How do you see its foundations? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful are they, and how severe is their ability. He said: How do you see its branches? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful are they, and how severe is their heaping. He said: How do you see its black smoke? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful is it, and how severe is its blackness. He said: Then how do you see its circle? They said: O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful is it, and how severe is its roundness. He said: Then how do you see its lightning, is it hidden, or a blink, or does it cut (through like) a cutting? They said: O Messenger of Allah, rather, that it cuts (through like a) cutting. Then the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Fertility (for the soil). Then they said: O Messenger of Allah, how fluent tare you, and we have not see anyone more fluent than you. He then said: And what will prevent me from that, when it is in my tongue that the Qur’an was sent down, in a clear Arabic tongue?
